# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the EXACT tasks you broke/fixed) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — seed: make the mid-tier reader ACTUALLY run+verify, and add compute tools for the hard-zero clusters
- Changes I made (1 line per edit; file/tool + cluster):
  - docx/scripts/fill_template.py (NEW): split-run {{placeholder}} + conditional filler, recurses nested tables + all headers/footers, self-verifies 0 placeholders remain — offer-letter-generator.
  - docx/SKILL.md: Execution contract + "run bundled filler then verify" + trigger keywords — offer-letter-generator.
  - pptx/scripts/replace.py: bullet branch emits <a:buAutoNum type=…> on numbered/bullet_type/bullet_char (else unchanged) — pptx-reference-formatting.
  - pptx/SKILL.md: Execution contract + editing rules (center=paragraph algn, buAutoNum not "1.", pick TITLE placeholder, embedded-object pointer) — pptx-reference-formatting.
  - pptx/embedded_objects.md (NEW): worked example editing ppt/embeddings/*.xlsx in place, preserving formula cells — exceltable-in-ppt.
  - xlsx/scripts/create_pivot.py (NEW): add_pivot_table() builds a real PivotTable (ws._pivots[0]) — sales-pivot-analysis.
  - xlsx/scripts/reconcile.py (NEW): suffix-aware fuzzy vendor match + id/amount normalization — invoice-fraud-detection.
  - xlsx/SKILL.md: Execution contract, mandatory python3 recalc + verify, read-rules-first, join preservation, missing-value recovery, real-pivot/reconcile pointers; python→python3 — weighted-gdp-calc, reserves-at-risk-calc, xlsx-recover-data, financial-modeling-qa, sales-pivot, invoice-fraud.
- Expected effect + why safe: dominant root cause across all 9 was advice-mode (agent never writes/recalcs/verifies the graded file). Contracts make the produce-file + recalc + verify steps unmissable; the four new scripts/reference close hard-zero capability gaps (real pivot object, split-run template fill, fuzzy reconciliation, in-place embedded-xlsx edit) that no prose could fix for a 0.00 task. Safe because 0 tasks currently pass (no passing behavior to regress); all script additions are additive and the pptx buAutoNum path is gated on new JSON props so default bullet output is byte-identical.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none — seed iteration, no prior entries/RESULT lines.
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: none deliberately deferred; every controllable cluster got an edit. Residual risk is whether the mid-tier reader honors the contract and actually invokes the bundled scripts — if RESULT shows tasks still 0 with the file absent, the next lever is to make the scripts the ONLY documented path (remove alternative inline recipes) and add a one-command copy-paste invocation per task type.
- Plateau signal: n/a (first iteration).
- Focus next iteration: read the RESULT/broke/fixed below; for any cluster still 0, check the trace for whether the script was called at all (behavioral) vs called-but-wrong-output (tool bug), and switch lever accordingly.

> **RESULT (framework, objective):** REJECTED (champion unchanged) · val=0.000 Δ=+0.000 · fixed={—} · broke={—}. — its WHOLE batch was reverted; re-introduce only the edits that did NOT break a task above, dropping/redesigning the ones that did.

## Iteration cand_0002 — verified, locally-tested skill-body fixes (docx filler consolidated; xlsx recalc knowledge; pptx recipes)
- Changes I made (1 line per edit; file/tool + cluster):
  - docx/SKILL.md: replaced 5 competing code snippets with ONE tested filler + execution contract + widened trigger description — offer-letter-generator (placeholders left in tables/nested tables/split runs).
  - docx/scripts/fill_template.py (rewritten): split-run + nested-table + header/footer + multi-paragraph {{IF}} + case-insensitive/nested-JSON key match + self-verify 0 remain.
  - xlsx/SKILL.md: NEW front-loaded MANDATORY workflow — "openpyxl leaves cached values None ⇒ verifier data_only reads None ⇒ must `python3 recalc.py` then re-open data_only and confirm no None"; fixed all bare `python `→`python3 ` — weighted-gdp-calc, reserves-at-risk-calc, financial-modeling-qa, xlsx-recover-data, sales-pivot (formula-value half).
  - pptx/SKILL.md: verified python-pptx recipes (center=PP_ALIGN.CENTER, ordered bullets=<a:buAutoNum>, font Arial/16/not-bold/#hex, bottom-center) + execution/verify contract + embedded-xlsx edit recipe; trimmed 18→5 palettes and design lists to stay <500 lines — pptx-reference-formatting, exceltable-in-ppt.
- Expected effect + why safe: 0/10 pass now, so NO passing task can regress — every edit's blast radius is nil by construction; the only bar is the significance gate. docx fix is the highest-confidence flip (verified end-to-end locally on a template reproducing the exact failure). xlsx/pptx fixes target the exact diagnosed mechanisms (None cached values; wrong alignment/bullet XML; missing output file).
- Building on prior RESULTS: cand_0001 REJECTED fixed={} broke={} — its scripts+contracts+description batch moved nothing. I did NOT simply re-submit it. Difference: (a) every fix verified locally before shipping; (b) the docx solution lives INLINE in the body (reliable channel) consolidated to a single path, not only in a possibly-unreachable script; (c) added the specific KNOWLEDGE gap (openpyxl None cached values) and verified pptx XML recipes rather than louder generic contracts.
- Refuted hypotheses: cand_0001 showed that bundled scripts + generic "run it & verify" contracts alone (without verified body content / specific knowledge) do NOT move any task — do not re-test that shape.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: domain-reasoning errors — financial-modeling-qa (wrong computed answer), invoice-fraud-detection (wrong fraud criteria/output), weighted-gdp/reserves data-mapping. A skill cannot supply these answers without task-specific hardcoding (overfit). Designs tried: none viable via skill edits.
- Plateau signal: only 2 iterations; if cand_0002 also nets ~0 despite verified mechanical fixes, the signal is that skill-body content is NOT reaching/steering the mid-tier agent (triggering or non-adherence) — next lever would be the description/trigger and radical body shortening, or confirming whether bundled scripts are even on the runtime disk.
- Focus next iteration: read RESULT below; if docx still fails, check the trace for whether the new filler/inline code was used at all (adherence) vs used-but-wrong (tool bug), and switch lever accordingly.
